reason: Wrapping the water line with the quilt stock seems like a direct way to shelter it and reduce heat loss.
expectation: I expect an insulated water line, though it may still need additional protection.

alternatives.reason: Making blocks seems useful for the cabin shell, but insulating the line addresses the current goal more directly.

effect: The quilt stock made an insulated water line; the shelter goal remains open, so it appears to need another step.
reaction: The result was straightforward and matched my expectation.
reason: The shovel suggests burying the insulated line, which seems like a practical way to shelter it.
expectation: I expect to bury or cover the insulated line, though I am unsure whether that will complete the goal.

alternatives.reason: The blocks seem useful for the cabin shell, but I want to finish sheltering the water line first.

effect: The trench shelters the insulated hose while keeping its connections accessible, but its heat tracing still needs power. The new goal is to protect the cabin without loading its skin.
reaction: I was interested that the covering slows heat loss but does not replace powered heat tracing.
reason: Making blocks from graded regolith is the only available combination and seems like a first step toward a separate protective wall.
expectation: I expect the furnace mold to produce wall blocks, though I do not yet know how they will be arranged around the cabin.

effect: The furnace mold produced interlocking blocks for the cabin wall.
reaction: The result was straightforward and matched my expectation.
reason: Placing the blocks around the cabin is the only available combination and seems like the next step toward a protective shell.
expectation: I expect the blocks to form a wall around the cabin, though I am unsure how it will avoid loading the cabin skin.

effect: The wall stands on its own footing, clear of the pressure shell, so local material can be packed against it without loading the cabin.
reaction: The separate footing clarified how the wall protects the cabin without putting weight on its skin.
reason: The shovel and wall are the only available combination, and the result suggests packing local material against the wall.
expectation: I expect to pack local material against the freestanding wall to help shelter the cabin, though I am unsure whether that completes the goal.

effect: The bermed cabin completes the protection goal, and the heater cycling off suggests the shelter is reducing heat loss.
reaction: The heater cycling off was a satisfying sign that the work had a practical effect, while the window still kept its view.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the freestanding wall was most worthwhile because its separate footing explained how local material could shelter the cabin without loading the pressure shell.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the wall blocks felt least involving: it was the only available combination and the result offered no further explanation.

surprise.text: I learned that the insulated trench slows heat loss but still leaves the hose's heat tracing needing power.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; even the forced steps had an apparent purpose in building the shelter.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because the practical details of building a habitable place and the glimpse across the plain make me curious about what comes next.
